questions.q: What does the summary say clutter costs the average worker each year?
a: About a full work week spent searching for things
About two hours of lost meetings
Roughly a month of paid leave
Nearly half of all email time
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites estimates of a whole work week lost to searching for items.

questions.q: What three kinds of joy should decide whether an item stays?
a: Immediate joy, functional joy and future joy
Shared joy, private joy and public joy
Daily joy, weekly joy and yearly joy
Cheap joy, lasting joy and earned joy
questions.why: Lesson 2 says discard anything that offers none of these three.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest sorting paperwork?
a: Into pending, requirement and desire piles
Into urgent, optional and archived piles
By client, date and project
By color, size and sender
questions.why: Lesson 2 gives those three categories for the papers in your workspace.

questions.q: What two desktop folders does the summary recommend creating?
a: A storage folder for old files and a current folder for active ones
A work folder and a personal folder
An inbox folder and an archive folder
A drafts folder and a final folder
questions.why: Lesson 3 says old files go to storage and active project files to current.

questions.q: What email habit does the summary recommend?
a: Treat email as current work and keep ten or fewer folders
Keep every message in the inbox for future reference
Create a separate folder for each frequent sender
Answer each message the moment it arrives
questions.why: Lesson 3 says email is for current projects, not storage, and fewer folders is better.
